difference between ACH and EFT in Canada?

In Canada they're mostly the same thing; 'ACH' is the US term.
- EFT (electronic funds transfer) is the Canadian name for batch bank-to-bank debits and credits, cleared through Payments Canada's ACSS (now moving to Lynx and the Real-Time Rail)
- ACH is the US equivalent network run by Nacha and the Fed
- Pre-authorized debits (PADs) are the Canadian version of ACH debits, governed by Payments Canada Rule H1
So for a Canadian merchant, 'EFT' is the right word; 'ACH' only fits if the money moves through the US system.
why are the maples on our street already red when the ones by the lake are still green?

Mostly stress and light. Red comes from anthocyanins, which maples make when sugars build up in leaves on sunny days followed by cool nights. Street trees have it rougher: compacted soil, heat from the pavement and drought stress make them colour and drop earlier. Trees near the lake stay milder at night, so they turn later.

events.text: =VLOOKUP(A2,Merchants!A:D,4) pulls the wrong merchant's plan on some rows. what's wrong

It's missing the exact-match flag. Without a fourth argument, VLOOKUP does an approximate match and assumes column A is sorted, so it grabs the nearest smaller ID.
- Fix: =VLOOKUP(A2,Merchants!A:D,4,FALSE)
- Or switch to =XLOOKUP(A2,Merchants!A:A,Merchants!D:D,"not found"), which defaults to exact match and doesn't break if columns move
- Also check for trailing spaces in the IDs; wrap with TRIM() if some still miss
rule of thumb for calling a cohort retention curve 'flattened'?

Call it flat when the period-over-period drop stays under about 1 to 2 percentage points for three or more periods in a row.
- Look at several cohorts together; one flat cohort can be noise
- Plot on the same axis from period 0 so you compare like with like
- If newer cohorts flatten higher than older ones, the product is improving; if they flatten lower, acquisition quality is slipping
- For payments products, weekly active processing is a better signal than logins

Diego's partner wants a daycare spot in the Annex for their toddler, keeps hearing about waitlists. how do Toronto daycare waitlists work?

Mostly centre by centre, through the City's central waitlist.
- Families register once on the City of Toronto Child Care Wait List and pick up to about 10 centres; there's no fee to join
- Each centre fills spots from its own list, usually by sign-up date, with priority for siblings and staff
- Infant and toddler spots are the scarcest; 12 to 18 months of waiting is common in the Annex
- Calling the directors every couple of months genuinely helps, because spots open with little notice
- Under the $10-a-day program (CWELCC), most licensed centres now charge about $22 a day, falling further over time

where does pastel de nata come from? Leo has questions

From the Jerónimos Monastery in Belém, Lisbon. Monks used egg whites to starch clothes and baked the leftover yolks into custard tarts. When the monasteries closed in 1834, they sold the recipe to a nearby sugar refinery, which opened the Pastéis de Belém bakery in 1837. It still uses the secret recipe.
